title: add-jsonschema-strict-mode-response_format-and-validation-openai-compat
author: Ava Thompson
release_notes: Add server-side JSON Schema response_format with strict mode and improved validation errors; OpenAI-compatibility mapping for response_format and structured error payloads.
description: Motivation: Customer adoption of structured outputs and tool/function calling has revealed gaps in server-side JSON Schema enforcement, inconsistent error messages, and incompatibilities with OpenAI-compatible response_format usage. This PR adds a first-class server-side JSON Schema validator for response_format, a strict mode that enforces exact schema conformance for generated outputs, improved structured error reporting for validation failures, and compatibility shims for the OpenAI-style response_format schema field. The change is intentionally opt-in via the existing response_format API and a new response_format.strict boolean so we do not break existing users. High-level changes: 1) API: response_format now accepts an optional "strict" flag (true|false). When strict=true the runtime will reject outputs that do not conform to the provided JSON Schema and return a structured validation error rather than best-effort. 2) Validation: integrate ajv-based server validator for JS runtimes and a shared schema validation layer in the inference API so behavior is consistent across node/go/python backends. 3) Errors: structured error payloads include path, schema keyword, message, original_output and a normalized openai_compat field for clients that expect OpenAI-like error shapes. 4) SDKs/docs: types and examples updated in redwood-sdk-python and redwood-sdk-typescript; docs updated with migration guide and examples for function/tool-calling + response_format strict combination. 5) Tests: unit tests, integration tests with streaming edge-cases, and e2e tests against OpenAI-compat layer. Checklist: - [x] Add server-side validation layer and schema registry hooks - [x] Implement response_format.strict handling and defaulting behavior - [x] Return structured validation errors with normalized openai_compat keys - [x] Update SDKs and examples (Python/TS) - [x] Add unit/integration/e2e tests, including streaming and function-calling combos - [x] Update docs and release notes Compatibility notes: default behavior remains best-effort (strict=false) to preserve existing responses. Enabling strict mode may cause previously-accepted outputs to be rejected; customers should test with the validation tooling and use canary rollouts. Metrics/observability: added validation.failure.* metrics and a per-route validation_latency histogram. CI: initial CI run showed a lint failure in the TS SDK which was fixed in a follow-up commit; full test suite passed on the final run. Related: ENG-4821 (schema validator refactor), ENG-5010 (openai-compat mapping for response_format).
